events.text:
⚡️🇩🇪🇱🇹 Reuters: Germany's army has begun its first tactical tests of kamikaze drones in Lithuania, along with Helsing's AI based targeting software Clarity. The drone tests took place on Sunday during Freedom Shield, Germany's largest military drills in the country to date.
Army chief Lieutenant General Christian Freuding watched loitering munitions made by German companies Helsing and Stark, fitted with inert warheads, hit main battle tanks at the Rudninkai training ground near the Belarusian border. Days earlier, troops there tested Clarity, which processes data from satellites, drones and other sensors and recommends actions to commanders. Freuding described both kinds of systems as essential to modern warfare.
Germany only decided in 2025 to buy loitering munitions. An armoured brigade of 5,000 German troops will be stationed permanently in Lithuania by the end of 2027, with about 1,800 already deployed there.

events.text:
🇮🇷🚢 Iran bans dozens of tugboats for violating Strait of Hormuz transit rules
The Persian Gulf Strait Authority (PGSA), an Iranian body regulating passage through the Strait of Hormuz, has blacklisted 26 tugboats for servicing vessels that violated transit rules.
The blacklist was drawn up based on tip-offs from citizens in Iran’s southern neighboring countries, as well as Iranian intelligence gathered through field operations and surveillance.
👉 Founded in April 2026 following the US-Israeli invasion, the PGSA was tasked with restricting cargo traffic through the strait. Since, cargo vessels have been able to pass safely only in coordination with the authority.
In an attempt to circumvent the restrictions, the US resorted to risky ship-to-ship transfers, with shuttle vessels operating at night, switching off their transponders and disabling their GPS signals for hours at a time.
The scheme has also proved costly. The daily charter rate for a Very Large Crude Carrier (VLCC) has surged from $231,400 to more than $1 million. The US must also maintain a military naval presence in the region to oversee the operation.
Yet unauthorized tankers keep catching fire in the strait.
Iran has laid out a set of conditions for reopening the waterway and is calling on the US to comply.

🇸🇦 Saudi Arabia seeks missile interceptors around the world 
The Saudis have reached out to several countries in search of anti-drone weapon systems and missiles, Semafor reports, citing its sources.
Among the nations contacted by Saudi Arabia were the US, the UK and France, as well as “countries from the Americas to Asia.”
It is unclear whether these inquiries are the result of the Saudi missile interceptor stockpiles running low or a sign of Saudi Arabia preparing for a protracted conflict in the region.
During this year, Saudi Arabia came under repeated drone and missile strikes by the Houthis who seek reprisals for the brutal military campaign waged by them and their proxies in Yemen.
The Iranian military also carried out missile and attacks against the Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia due to the facility being used by the US forces.
